purpose: Supplemental personal-investment research candidates sourced from transcript idea generation, thematic expansion and daily Power Stack sweeps. Inclusion and scoring are based on primary company disclosures and regulatory filings where available, with current third-party reporting used only to bridge newly reported results that are not yet indexed on issuer pages.

ideas.name: Hubbell
ideas.theme: Utility T&D + electrical solutions + data-centre balance of system
ideas.thesis: Hubbell is a differentiated grid-modernisation and electrification supplier with exposure to utility transmission, substations, distribution and electrical balance-of-system products. It participates in data-centre load growth without depending on one hyperscaler, GPU platform or power-generation technology.
ideas.catalysts: Multi-year utility T&D investment, data-centre-driven transmission/substation demand, strong Electrical Solutions growth, capacity additions and continued guidance upgrades.
ideas.risks: Premium valuation, raw-material/tariff inflation, margin pressure from growth investments and a slowdown in utility or data-centre capex.
ideas.valuationTechnical: Quality and end-market visibility justify a premium, but entry price still matters. Prefer pullbacks or periods where earnings revisions outpace multiple expansion rather than chasing grid-theme momentum.
ideas.researchNote: Q2 2026 net sales rose 15% with 10% organic growth and adjusted EPS rose 12%. Utility Solutions had a roughly 1.2x first-half book-to-bill, with management citing particular order and quoting strength in transmission and substations from load growth and data-centre buildouts. FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $20.25-$20.55.

ideas.name: Powell Industries
ideas.theme: Switchgear + engineered power distribution + data-centre electrical systems
ideas.thesis: Powell is a relatively pure electrical-distribution bottleneck play spanning medium- and low-voltage switchgear, substations, modular power-control rooms and integrated power systems. It adds differentiated exposure versus GEV/HUBB/ETN because it is smaller, engineered-to-order and directly levered to complex data-centre, utility, LNG and heavy-industrial electrical projects.
ideas.catalysts: Conversion of the record backlog, the >$400m mega data-centre award, continued utility/LNG/data-centre order wins, Houston capacity expansion, Remsdaq/SCADA cross-selling and sustained book-to-bill above 1x.
ideas.risks: Premium valuation, project timing and revenue-conversion volatility, execution on an unusually large backlog, customer/project concentration, labour and component constraints, and sharp multiple compression if order growth normalises.
ideas.valuationTechnical: The business quality and backlog justify a premium, but this is not a cheap electrical-equipment stock. The post-earnings volatility is useful for entry discipline; avoid treating record orders as straight-line revenue or permanent margins.
ideas.researchNote: Official Q2 FY2026 results showed revenue +6%, new orders +97% to $490m, backlog +33% to $1.8bn and a subsequent data-centre order above $400m. Current reporting on fiscal Q3 indicates revenue around $311.7m, record new orders around $934m, roughly 3.0x book-to-bill and backlog near $2.4bn, while EPS/revenue missed consensus. The combination is attractive: demand is exceptional, but execution and valuation risk are real enough to keep conviction below GEV/ETN/HUBB.

ideas.name: Ecolab
ideas.theme: Water treatment + ultrapure water + direct liquid cooling for AI data centres
ideas.thesis: Ecolab is one of the cleanest ways to combine water scarcity, industrial water treatment and AI-data-centre cooling in one platform. The CoolIT acquisition adds direct liquid cooling to an existing water-technology franchise that already serves semiconductor fabs, power generation and industrial customers.
ideas.catalysts: CoolIT integration, >100% year-to-date CoolIT sales growth, Global High-Tech expansion, data-centre liquid-cooling adoption, semiconductor ultrapure-water demand and rising water-efficiency requirements.
ideas.risks: $4.75bn acquisition execution, premium valuation, integration risk, temporary margin dilution from acquired businesses and the possibility that hyperscaler cooling architectures become more vertically integrated.
ideas.valuationTechnical: The thematic quality is exceptional, but the acquisition premium means entry price matters. Prefer periods where earnings revisions and CoolIT growth validate the multiple rather than buying solely on the AI-water narrative.
ideas.researchNote: Ecolab closed the CoolIT Systems acquisition in July 2026 for about $4.75bn. CoolIT year-to-date sales were growing more than 100%. Ecolab now spans ultrapure water for chip fabrication, water systems for power generation and direct liquid cooling for high-density AI data centres. Q2 2026 reported sales grew 10%, organic sales 5%, and the company raised its adjusted EPS outlook.

ideas.name: Modine
ideas.theme: Data-centre thermal management + chillers + climate solutions
ideas.thesis: Modine is becoming a much cleaner data-centre cooling pure play as it separates Performance Technologies and concentrates capital on Climate Solutions. It has direct exposure to the thermal-management bottleneck created by higher rack densities and AI compute.
ideas.catalysts: $4bn long-term chiller agreement with a hyperscale customer, capacity expansion, data-centre cooling sales growth, Climate Solutions becoming the core company and continued margin scaling after expansion costs normalise.
ideas.risks: Customer concentration, aggressive capacity expansion, temporary margin pressure, execution risk around the portfolio separation and dependence on sustained hyperscaler capex.
ideas.valuationTechnical: Higher-beta than ECL or XYL but with more direct upside to AI cooling. Treat as a growth industrial: strong order visibility is attractive, but avoid assuming current triple-digit data-centre growth rates persist indefinitely.
ideas.researchNote: Fiscal 2026 Q4 data-centre sales increased 158% year over year. Climate Solutions sales rose 87%, and Modine disclosed a landmark $4bn long-term chiller agreement with a major hyperscale customer. Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for 20%-35% sales growth and 38%-44% adjusted EBITDA growth.

sources.label: Modine portfolio separation and Climate Solutions focus

ideas.name: Xylem
ideas.theme: Water infrastructure + treatment + reuse + industrial water security
ideas.thesis: Xylem is the broad water-infrastructure picks-and-shovels exposure: utilities, industrial users, treatment, reuse, metering and network efficiency. Data-centre growth strengthens the case because AI increases competition for water and makes reuse and smart-water infrastructure more valuable.
ideas.catalysts: Utility capex, industrial water reuse, stricter water-efficiency standards, AI/data-centre water demand, municipal leakage reduction and continued order growth.
ideas.risks: Public-sector project timing, premium defensive-infrastructure valuation, integration/execution risk and slower revenue conversion despite strong order growth.
ideas.valuationTechnical: Lower thematic beta than MOD but a much broader moat and lower AI dependency. Best treated as a long-duration water-security compounder rather than a short-term AI trade.
ideas.researchNote: Q2 2026 orders reached $3.1bn, up 42% reported and 41% organically, while revenue was $2.3bn. Xylem explicitly identifies AI-driven water demand and water reuse as strategic growth drivers and argues that smart-water infrastructure and reuse can expand supply for data-centre demand without simply drawing more fresh water.

ideas.name: Valmont Industries
ideas.theme: Precision irrigation + water efficiency + grid infrastructure crossover
ideas.thesis: Valmont is a useful two-sided Power Stack holding: irrigation and precision-agriculture systems improve water productivity, while its larger infrastructure business participates in utility-grid investment. That makes it a better diversified agriculture/water expression than a pure farm-equipment cycle bet.
ideas.catalysts: Recovery in irrigation demand, drought/water-efficiency investment, precision-ag adoption, international irrigation projects and continued utility-infrastructure growth.
ideas.risks: Agriculture remains cyclical and currently soft, farm-income pressure can delay irrigation upgrades, Middle East disruptions hurt international demand and steel costs affect margins.
ideas.valuationTechnical: Current agriculture weakness is both the risk and potential entry setup. The stronger infrastructure segment reduces downside versus a pure irrigation manufacturer, but conviction should rise only when irrigation volumes stabilise.
ideas.researchNote: Q2 2026 total sales rose 6.5%, but Agriculture sales fell 15.8% amid market softness and Middle East disruption. The investment case is therefore counter-cyclical rather than momentum-driven: long-run water-efficiency need remains intact while the grid-infrastructure business provides support.

ideas.name: Corteva
ideas.thesis: Corteva is a direct agricultural-productivity platform spanning seeds, traits and crop protection. The long-run thesis is not simply higher food prices; it is that constrained land, water and climate variability increase the value of yield-enhancing genetics and crop-protection technology.
ideas.catalysts: Seed pricing and technology adoption, new crop-protection products, operational leverage, the planned October 2026 separation and higher demand for farm productivity under resource constraints.
ideas.risks: Crop-price weakness, farmer affordability, regulatory pressure on crop-protection products, weather variability, separation execution and pricing competition.
ideas.valuationTechnical: A higher-quality agriculture exposure than commodity processors because value creation comes from intellectual property and product innovation. The planned separation adds event risk and potential rerating optionality.
ideas.researchNote: Corteva reported strong first-half 2026 operating performance and raised full-year guidance. Q2 organic sales were down 2%, but operating EBITDA rose 4% and operating EPS rose 5%; first-half operating EBITDA rose 10% and operating EPS 14%. The company remains on track for its planned October 1 separation.

ideas.name: Eli Lilly
ideas.thesis: Lilly is a direct beneficiary of the structural rise in obesity, type-2 diabetes and related cardiometabolic disease, but the thesis should be framed around disease burden, treatment penetration and drug efficacy rather than assuming poorer diets automatically create profits. Its tirzepatide franchise currently has exceptional demand and pipeline depth.
ideas.catalysts: Continued Mounjaro/Zepbound volume growth, broader reimbursement, international expansion, oral obesity products, retatrutide and manufacturing-capacity expansion.
ideas.risks: Very high expectations and valuation, pricing/reimbursement pressure, competition from Novo and future entrants, concentration in incretin drugs, safety/regulatory risk and political scrutiny of drug pricing.
ideas.valuationTechnical: Fundamental growth is exceptional, but much of the obesity opportunity is already recognised by the market. Treat as a high-quality growth compounder where entry price and pipeline execution matter more than simply extrapolating prevalence trends.
ideas.researchNote: Q2 2026 revenue rose about 48% to $23bn. Mounjaro generated about $9.94bn and Zepbound about $4.93bn, and Lilly raised full-year revenue guidance to $85-$87bn. The concentration makes the upside powerful but also raises franchise risk.

ideas.name: Dexcom
ideas.thesis: Dexcom is a picks-and-shovels way to own diabetes and metabolic-health management rather than betting only on pharmaceuticals. Continuous glucose monitoring can expand beyond insulin-dependent diabetes into broader type-2 diabetes and metabolic-health use cases as monitoring becomes cheaper and more mainstream.
ideas.catalysts: CGM penetration in non-insulin type-2 diabetes, reimbursement expansion, international growth, new sensors and evidence that CGM improves outcomes in broader populations.
ideas.risks: Competition from Abbott and other sensor platforms, reimbursement pressure, product quality issues, hardware commoditisation and slower consumer adoption outside core diabetes populations.
ideas.valuationTechnical: More execution-sensitive than LLY but less dependent on one drug franchise. Attractive when adoption growth and margin expansion are visible without requiring speculative consumer-wellness assumptions.
ideas.researchNote: Q2 2026 revenue grew 13% to $1.308bn; U.S. revenue grew 11% and international revenue 19%. GAAP operating margin expanded to 24.3%. Dexcom also reported positive randomized trial results showing clinically meaningful glucose-control improvement in people with type-2 diabetes not using insulin.

notes: SpaceX remains a personal-investment research candidate evaluated on fundamentals, valuation, capital intensity and risk.
Water / Cooling is now a first-class diversification theme covering municipal and industrial water infrastructure, water reuse, ultrapure process water and data-centre thermal management.
Agriculture / Food Systems is evaluated through productivity, water efficiency, seed/trait technology and food-system resilience rather than simple commodity-price bets.

Healthcare / Metabolic focuses on the structural burden of obesity, type-2 diabetes and cardiometabolic disease, while avoiding deterministic assumptions that lower-quality diets automatically translate into investment returns.
Daily-sweep additions must improve diversification or bottleneck exposure rather than simply increase ticker count.
